predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the Bhopal State of 17,876 km2 (1901): the present-day Bhopal, Raisen and Sehore districts

successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: the Bhopal State of 17,876 km2 (1901): the present-day Bhopal, Raisen and Sehore districts

ledger.x: 1707: Dost Mohammad Khan founds Bhopal State.
1709: Dost Mohammad Khan takes the lease of the Berasia estate.
1728: the capital moves from Bhopal to Islamnagar.
1742: the capital returns from Islamnagar to Bhopal.
1 June 1949: the Union Government of India takes over Bhopal.

wars.name: Battle of Bhopal
wars.outcome: On 24 December 1737 Baji Rao beat the Mughal forces under Nizam-ul-Mulk, with the Nawab of Bhopal among the vassal belligerents; the peace of 7 January 1738 (Treaty of Bhopal, signed at Doraha) gave the Marathas Malwa and 50 lakh rupees; the page is silent on…

wars.name: Nizam-ul-Mulk invasion of Bhopal
wars.outcome: The Nizam invaded in March 1724 and forced Dost Mohammad Khan to cede much of his territory.

certainty.note: The pages give the 1901 area and the three districts only; the shape is a box of that area for all years.
